sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: A Full-Thickness Macular Hole (FTMH) is a foveal dehiscence involving all retinal layers from the internal limiting membrane (ILM) to the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). It typically results from tangential and anteroposterior vitreous traction at the macula.

sections.title: Red Flags: Emergency Signs
content: Metamorphopsia (Amsler grid distortion)
Central scotoma expansion
Sudden drop in BCVA
Associated Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment (RRD)

content.explanation: Metamorphopsia (wavy lines), Amsler grid distortion, Central vision loss, Unilateral symptoms, Loss of contrast sensitivity, Aching (minimal/none).

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: Step 1: BCVA - Usually 20/70 to 20/200.
Step 2: Amsler Grid testing - Reveal central metamorphopsia.
Step 3: Slit-Lamp Biomicroscopy - Watzke-Allen test (positive).
Step 4: SD-OCT - Gold standard to confirm hole diameter and integrity of EZ (Ellipsoid Zone).

sections.title: Surgical Management Protocol
content: Step 1: Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) - 23/25/27 Gauge.
Step 2: Induction of PVD - Vital for releasing traction.
Step 3: Internal Limiting Membrane (ILM) Peeling - Use of Brilliant Blue G or Indocyanine Green (ICG).
Step 4: Fluid-Air Exchange.
Step 5: Tamponade - C3F8 (14%) or SF6 (20%) gas.
Step 6: Face-down positioning - Essential for 3-5 days.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Closure rates exceed 90-95% for most primary macular holes.
Inverted ILM flap technique is preferred for chronic or large (>400um) holes.
Post-operative BCVA improvement is highly dependent on the integrity of the Ellipsoid Zone (EZ) on OCT.
Risk of cataract progression is nearly 100% following gas tamponade.

sections.title: Recent Advances
sections.content: Recent landmark trends emphasize the use of autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) or amniotic membrane grafts for refractory macular holes. Additionally, studies on micro-incision vitrectomy (MIVS) demonstrate faster recovery times and reduced inflammation.

sections.title: --- Sub-topics from: Mastering the Macular Hole: From Pathogenesis to Post-Op ---
sections.content: A comprehensive clinical deep-dive into Full-Thickness Macular Holes (FTMH), covering the evolution of staging from Gass to IVTS, gold-standard diagnostic maneuvers, and the nuances of vitreoretinal surgical management.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: A Full-Thickness Macular Hole (FTMH) is a primary neurosensory retinal defect involving all layers from the internal limiting membrane (ILM) to the outer segments of the photoreceptors. It typically occurs at the fovea centralis, leading to a significant loss of central visual acuity and metamorphopsia. While most are idiopathic and related to age-related vitreoretinal interface changes, they can also be secondary to trauma or high myopia.

sections.title: The Gass Staging System (Historical Gold Standard)

rows: Central yellow spot; loss of foveal reflex.
Central yellow ring; further elevation of the foveola.
Small eccentric break in the foveal floor; 'can-opener' tear.
Large hole with cuff of subretinal fluid; No Weiss Ring.
Large hole; Weiss ring present on biomicroscopy.

sections.title: Pathophysiology: The Gass Theory
content: 1. Perifoveal Vitreous Detachment begins.
2. Focal tangential traction at the fovea by the posterior hyaloid.
3. Cystic changes occur in the foveolar layers (Stage 1).
4. Centrifugal migration of photoreceptors.
5. Full-thickness dehiscence and centripetal retraction of retinal edges.

sections.title: Clinical Features & Symptoms
content: Progressive decrease in central vision (usually 20/80 to 20/400).
Metamorphopsia: Distorted lines on Amsler Grid.
Central Scotoma: A 'hole' in the center of vision.
Micropsia: Objects appearing smaller.
Typically painless and unilateral onset.

sections.title: Diagnostic Ocular Examination
content: Watzke-Allen Sign: Slit beam over hole is perceived as thinned or broken.
Laser Beam Test: 50um spot disappears into the hole.
Biomicroscopy: Round, red lesion with yellow-white deposits (drusen-like) at the base.
Cuff of Subretinal Fluid: Surrounding the hole edges.
Pseudo-operculum: Suspended tissue over the hole (condensed vitreous).

rows: Verticalized foveal edges; no tissue loss.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: 1. Spectral Domain OCT (SD-OCT): The gold standard for sizing and staging.
2. Amsler Grid: To document the area of metamorphopsia.
3. Fundus Fluorescein Angiography (FFA): Shows 'window defect' early, but rarely necessary.
4. Microperimetry: Maps the depth and extent of the central scotoma.
5. Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Increased autofluorescence in the hole due to RPE unmasking.

sections.title: Surgical Management Protocol
content: 1. Pars Plana Vitrectomy (23G, 25G, or 27G).
2. Induction of Posterior Vitreous Detachment (PVD) if not present.
3. ILM Peeling: Often aided by Brilliant Blue G (BBG) or Indocyanine Green (ICG).
4. Fluid-Air Exchange (FAX).
5. Gas Tamponade: Long-acting (C3F8) or short-acting (SF6).
6. Post-operative positioning: Face-down for 3-7 days (surgeon dependent).

sections.title: Red Flags & Urgent Considerations
content: Acute vision drop in the fellow eye (15% risk).
Signs of Endophthalmitis post-op (pain, hypopyon).
Iatrogenic retinal breaks during surgery.
Rapidly progressive cataract (common after vitrectomy).
Elevated Intraocular Pressure (IOP) from gas expansion.

content.explanation: Beam broken = Macular hole; Ray is bent = Pseudohole; Entirely normal = Malingering/Functional; All light seen = Lamellar hole; Kinked beam = Epiretinal membrane.

sections.title: Complications & Prognosis
content: Cataract formation (occurs in >75% within 2 years).
Retinal Detachment (1-2% risk).
Visual field defects (often related to air-fluid exchange).
RPE Toxicity (if ICG dye is used for ILM peeling).
Success Rate: >90% closure for Stage 2 holes.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Small holes (<250μm) have a higher chance of spontaneous closure (rare but documented).
Inverted ILM flap technique is superior for large holes (>400μm) and high myopia.
The presence of a Weiss ring confirms Stage 4 and reduces risk to the fellow eye.
OCT 'Base Diameter' is always larger than 'Minimum Linear Diameter' (MLD).

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
content: MIVS (Micro-Incision Vitrectomy Surgery): Reducing surgical trauma and recovery time.
Ocrplasmin (Jetrea): Pharmacologic vitreolysis for VMT, though use has declined due to limited efficacy in FTMH.
Autologous Retinal Flaps: For refractory or ultra-large holes.
Valved Cannulas: Maintaining stable IOP during ILM peeling.
Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) adjuvants: Exploring biological 'glue' for closure.

sections.title: Long-Term Monitoring Protocol
content: 1. Week 1: Check IOP and wound integrity.
2. Month 1: Monitor gas bubble resolution and OCT for closure.
3. Month 3: Assess visual acuity and metamorphopsia improvement.
4. Ongoing: Annual Amsler Grid monitoring of the fellow eye.
